news.title: What’s the latest on UK university compliance?
news.summary_en: This week, The PIE held the inaugural Compliance Con, bringing together compliance experts from across the UK sector. As tightened BCA thresholds loom, editor Beth Kennedy unpacks key takeaways from the event.
news.author: The PIE News team

news.title: Amaral Cunha, Escola Eleva
news.summary_en: This week, The PIE sat down with Amaral Cunha, head of school at Escola Eleva, part of Inspired Education Group. We spoke about his career to date and education's power to transform communities.
news.author: The PIE News team

news.title: Alphabetti spaghetti and Australia’s international education policy problem
news.summary_en: Neil Fitzroy explores how a growing maze of acronyms, restrictions and visa uncertainty may be undermining Australia's appeal as a study destination.
news.author: Neil Fitzroy

news.title: Student with gun demands deposit refund from agent
news.summary_en: A major study abroad agent has told The PIE it was forced to close offices in Pakistan for more than 10 days after a man with a gun demanded a refund of his  tuition fee deposit after being refused a visa to study in the UK.
news.author: Nicholas Cuthbert

news.title: Universities Australia warns against growing regulatory burden under Albanese reforms
news.summary_en: Universities Australia chief executive Luke Sheehy has warned that growing regulation and political intervention is weighing on universities, urging the new tertiary education commission to simplify oversight rather than add to it.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: German chancellor casts doubt on US study amid “different social climate”
news.summary_en: Friedrich Merz says he would not currently recommend young people study or work in the US, as debates around employability, stability and global student mobility intensify.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: UK study visa issuance falls 32%
news.summary_en: UK study visa issuance in Q1 2026 is down by a third compared to last year, as new government figures show net migration plummet.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Jacqui Smith hails UK ELT as English UK warns policy progress must not “stall”
news.summary_en: Skills minister Jacqui Smith has hailed English language teaching as a “very important strand” of the UK’s international education strategy, as English UK urges the government to accelerate reforms on youth mobility.
news.author: Kim Martin
